- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates momentum; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of early correction to forecast to align with sentiment shifts.
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply a 2–3% upward bias to forecast mean, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is high but price is declining, model often ignores sentiment; if sentiment >0.77 and price falls, add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast to reflect sentiment divergence.
